subject: Visual Arts
_width_axis_note: Width in visual arts varies by the range of materials, processes, styles, contexts and conceptual territories students engage with — not by phenomena in the science sense. A student at minimum width works with one material/process/context; wider students work across multiple, increasingly unfamiliar or self-directed contexts.

AC9AVA8C01.minimum_width: Generate and develop ideas for one artwork through at least two planning stages (e.g. brainstorm, compositional sketches); annotate choices using visual arts terminology.
AC9AVA8C01.typical_width: Generate, document and develop ideas across a unit using a visual arts journal or documentation system; make and justify compositional decisions; explore subject matter from multiple perspectives before committing to an approach.
wider: Develop ideas through sustained visual inquiry into a self-chosen subject or concept, experimenting with how perspective shifts the representation
Research and document how other artists have approached the same subject or theme; use findings to deliberately develop a distinct personal approach
Use Viewpoints to develop generative questions that push ideas into unexpected territory — document the thinking process as part of the artwork development
elaborations: engaging in visual brainstorming by selecting, organising and combining appropriate images, forms, visual art processes and materials to represent ideas about a particular subject
documenting their visual arts practice when developing ideas and processes, including studio practice, correct use of materials and tools, creative thinking and reflection
developing a series of compositional sketches as planning for a final artwork that communicates how the visual conventions and planned processes will communicate meaning
exploring and researching ideas about their interests in the world/subject matter or concepts from a particular perspective or a range of perspectives
recording and documenting their research into a subject or theme using their own images or images from other sources, written annotations and comments, or evaluations
exploring ways that artists, designers, architects or craftspeople communicate ideas and meaning in their work

AC9AVA8C02.minimum_width: Create one artwork that uses at least two visual conventions deliberately chosen to represent an idea, perspective or meaning; explain the choices made.
AC9AVA8C02.typical_width: Create artworks across the unit that demonstrate considered selection of visual conventions, processes and materials; explain how specific choices communicate intended meaning; document the decision-making process.
wider: Work across multiple media or processes (e.g. analog and digital, 2D and 3D) and evaluate how different material choices change what the artwork communicates
Create a work that uses digital tools (photographic manipulation, AR assets, digital drawing) and evaluate how digital processes extend or constrain expressive possibilities
Develop an artwork that explores a personally significant issue or emotional experience — reflect on how visual conventions carry meaning beyond literal representation
elaborations: creating a series of Augmented Reality digital assets that represent distinct textures, placing assets within a space to communicate concepts
creating artworks as a way of exploring feelings and emotions, such as self-awareness, emotional awareness and personal wellbeing
working independently and/or in groups to create artworks that tell stories or create awareness about issues significant to them
transforming an analog visual artwork into digital versions using digital tools; evaluating and selecting the most successful transformation
considering sustainable design practices when generating ideas — exploring sustainable fabrics and recycled materials when creating wearable art
applying knowledge of visual arts processes, materials and techniques to create artworks; demonstrating understanding of relief printing, digital tools etc.
representing ideas through considered use of visual conventions such as modulated lines to create movement, or breaking rhythmic patterns to create discord

AC9AVA8D01.minimum_width: Experiment with at least one visual convention, process or material to develop a specific skill; document outcomes and reflect on what the experimentation revealed.
AC9AVA8D01.typical_width: Experiment with a range of visual conventions, processes and materials across a unit; develop skills through deliberate practice; document and evaluate choices in a visual arts journal using appropriate terminology.
wider: Investigate how artists use encryption, layering or symbolic content in their artworks — experiment with these approaches in own work
Explore sustainable materials and processes (natural dyes, recycled materials) and reflect on how material constraints shape artistic decisions
Study how a specific artist uses a particular material or process and experiment with replicating and then diverging from that approach — document what is learned
elaborations: selecting and appropriately acknowledging the use of found images when making and responding to artworks
investigating the choices that other artists have made when structuring their representation of ideas
developing an understanding of how and why artists choose to use encryption in their artworks — analog and digital approaches
evaluating feedback from teachers and peers and documenting subsequent decisions in journals using visual arts terminology
developing an awareness of cultural and artistic conventions for representing subjects through contextual study, observing protocols for First Nations Australian cultural property
reflecting on learning and evaluating choices to represent their ideas as the artwork progresses
exploring the ways that a range of artists use materials and visual conventions to communicate concepts
observing the different ways that artists respond to sensory stimuli to generate ideas

AC9AVA8D02.minimum_width: Reflect on how at least one artist's use of visual conventions has influenced choices in own practice; document at least one specific decision that emerged from this reflection.
AC9AVA8D02.typical_width: Use teacher and student set goals to reflect on and practise specific skills over time; investigate how a specific artist or group of artists use materials and techniques to inform own practice; document the influence on decisions made.
wider: Develop an extended reflection on how multiple artists across different contexts have influenced own visual arts practice — trace how influences converge and diverge in own work
Explore sustainable material practices (natural dyes, ceramics firing decisions) and reflect on how sustainability considerations shape artistic choices
Investigate colour theory deeply (harmonious and contrasting palettes, emotional associations) and apply in a series of compositional experiments — document the reasoning at each stage
elaborations: developing understanding of the ways that visual conventions can be used to communicate feelings and emotions — exploring compositional sketches to identify how changes communicate different emotions
using teacher and student set goals to reflect on and practise specific skills over time, using Viewpoints to develop questions about aims, strengths and areas for improvement
exploring and reflecting on the way a particular artist uses materials, techniques and processes to inform own investigations
considering sustainable practices when exploring properties of materials
reflecting on the work of others and own explorations when developing an understanding of visual conventions and how they might be manipulated to communicate meaning
building on understanding of composition to explore multiple ways to represent space and depth — experimenting with proportion, scale, positive and negative space, perspective

AC9AVA8E01.minimum_width: Investigate how at least one artist uses visual conventions, processes or materials to represent ideas or meaning; describe the relationship between the artist's choices and the meaning communicated.
AC9AVA8E01.typical_width: Investigate artists from different times, places and/or cultures to analyse how visual conventions, processes and materials are manipulated to represent ideas; explain how context shapes meaning-making choices.
wider: Investigate First Nations Australian artworks that cross multiple artforms and analyse how visual, dramatic and musical elements combine to produce meaning
Research how artists across different cultural contexts represent the same subject (e.g. portraiture, natural world) — analyse what cultural conventions shape representation choices
Investigate the reciprocal influence between Australian and Asian artists and analyse how cross-cultural exchange shapes practice
elaborations: investigating arts works by First Nations Australian artists that cross over multiple artforms, analysing how the arts forms come together
researching the ways that artists from different times and places have represented a particular subject or theme
analysing the ways that artists represent subject matter and ideas in their artworks when developing ideas for own representations
creating written accounts such as catalogue entries or reviews that discuss how artists have shown their ideas
investigating and trialling techniques and visual arts processes used by artists, thinking about how processes have changed over time
exploring the ways that artists are inspired and influenced by the practice of artists from other countries or cultures

AC9AVA8E02.minimum_width: Identify at least one example where ICIP rights are relevant to visual arts practice; explain what respectful engagement looks like in that context.
AC9AVA8E02.typical_width: Investigate the diversity of First Nations Australian artworks and arts practices with attention to ICIP rights and protocols; analyse specific examples and explain how respectful approaches can be applied in own practice.
wider: Investigate a specific case of cultural appropriation in visual arts — identify what was denied, who was harmed, and what a respectful alternative would have looked like
Research how professional artists and design companies obtain permission to use cultural material belonging to a collective — apply this understanding to own decision-making
Explore how visual artists can use historical materials that accurately communicate First Nations perspectives while following ICIP protocols — develop own guidelines for practice
elaborations: locating and discussing information about ICIP rights and protocols, engaging in activities to understand how to make ethical choices
investigating examples of how visual artists and designers ensure their legal and moral obligations are met when selecting First Nations Australians' cultural material
investigating an example of cultural appropriation where ICIP rights have been denied and identifying how the situation could have been approached respectfully
exploring how visual artists can respect ICIP rights when using historical or background materials that communicate First Nations perspectives

AC9AVA8P01.minimum_width: Curate at least one artwork with accompanying documentation (label, statement or explanation) that communicates the ideas, perspectives or meaning behind the work to an audience.
AC9AVA8P01.typical_width: Curate and present examples of visual arts practice for an exhibition context; produce documentation that connects artworks to ideas and meaning; consider how the presentation space and curation choices affect audience experience.
wider: Create a themed series of artworks curated for display, developing a visual narrative through groupings and spatial decisions — use Viewpoints questions to guide curation choices
Create a digital presentation (webpage, walkthrough) to connect geographically distanced audiences with a visual arts showcase
Visit and critically evaluate an exhibition in a gallery or community site — use findings to inform own exhibition decisions
elaborations: creating a webpage, walkthrough, presentation or other document to connect geographically distanced audiences with a visual arts showcase
working together to identify/select a space within the school for showing their works, considering who in the community might see their works
visiting and evaluating exhibitions of work in galleries, museums or community sites and developing responses
making a themed series of artworks to be displayed in the class or via the school intranet, considering relationships between artworks and the space
creating visual art labels for an exhibition/showcase
describing the artistic vision of artists from different contexts, cultures, times and places
using hex editors to explore information included in encrypted artworks and create own encrypted information
